headline: A group of 420 scientists, including AI pioneers Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio, has asked that AI models able to carry out cyber attacks first be kept disconnected from the internet.
score_reason: Prominent signatories and a concrete ask, but an open letter with no deadline and no binding force.
importance_line: Governments, AI labs and the public would gain a clearer record of AI containment failures if the proposed international body is created, but the letter is only a request with no timetable.
summary: EdTech Innovation Hub reports that 420 scientists, among them Geoffrey Hinton of the University of Toronto, Yoshua Bengio of the Universite de Montreal and Stuart Russell of the University of California, Berkeley, signed an open letter asking organisations that build or test AI models capable of cyber attacks to keep them disconnected from the internet at first. The letter also proposes an international body to set containment standards and record failures, but gives no timetable and does not name the incidents it refers to.
notes: Full text read. The letter itself was not opened. Hinton, Bengio and Russell are named by the outlet as supporters.
